LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Melody
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Melody, part of Creating and Executing in Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How can interesting melodies be created?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. sing familiar songs based on the sol-fa syllables d r m, and identify the sol-fa syllables by ear,

2. listen to and identify aurally and orally the sol-fa pitches (d r m) as sounded on a melodic instrument/voice,

3. watch videos/demonstrations of execution of the Kodaly hand signs for the sol-fa syllables d, r m and practise performing the hand signs,

4. brainstorm on the qualities of a good melody,

5. apply composition techniques to create short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m and the note symbols; crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests,

6. collect clay for modelling from the local environment,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. sing familiar songs based on the sol-fa syllables d r m, and identify the sol-fa syllables by ear,
2. listen to and identify aurally and orally the sol-fa pitches (d r m) as sounded on a melodic instrument/voice,
3. watch videos/demonstrations of execution of the Kodaly hand signs for the sol-fa syllables d, r m and practise performing the hand signs,
4. brainstorm on the qualities of a good melody,
5. apply composition techniques to create short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m and the note symbols; crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests,
6. collect clay for modelling from the local environment,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Melody together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner uses unique and new ideas to compose melodies and models the sol-fa syllables.

• Self-efficacy: The learner models the sol-fa syllables and composes original melodies.

Values:
• Unity: The learner works with peers when modelling, creating and performing various melodies.

• Love: The learner respects others while critiquing their performances.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Life skills: The learner acquires interpersonal skills through interacting with peers in groups as they model sol-fa syllables

and create melodies.

• Mentorship and peer education: The learner shares their compositions with peers who give feedback for improvement.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner applies the skill of sequencing of sol-fa syllables when creating simple melodies using stepwise

motion.
